personality_one_liner: An intense, high-contrast, performance-oriented aesthetic that feels like a live operational surface for sports scouting.

spacing.rule: Handle spacing correctly dont have extra spaces where its not required, handle padding and margin corectly and subtle for buttons and components. Use sm/md spacing rhythm for a tight, dashboard-like feel.

do's: Use solid surfaceSecondary with exact elevation instead of glass, per Dark-First Utility.
dont's: No blur/glass effects. The UI must remain sharp and highly readable like a dashboard.

screens.name: Onboarding
screens.purpose: Dual-role selection screen to split the flow between Athletes and Recruiters.

states.error: Readable text in the center with a Retry button.

screens.layout: Two massive full-bleed image cards stacked vertically or presented sequentially. Each features a heavy vertical gradient scrim (transparent to 80% surfaceInverse) with a primary CTA pinned to the bottom. 'Je suis Athlète' vs 'Je suis Recruteur'.

screens.name: HomeFeed
screens.purpose: Recruiters see a vertical scrolling feed of athlete profile highlights; Athletes see recruitment offers from clubs.

states.loading: Skeleton of athlete cards or job offers.
states.empty: Illustration of a whistle/clipboard + 'Aucun profil trouvé pour l'instant' + 'Modifier les filtres' CTA.

screens.layout: High-impact, edge-to-edge profile cards. Each card uses an athlete photo with a heavy gradient-to-dark scrim. Athlete name and key stats (Speed, Position, Level) are overlaid using Barlow Condensed. For athletes, the feed shows club offers using surfaceSecondary cards.

screens.name: SearchFilters
screens.purpose: Granular search to filter athletes by sport, position, age, and skill level.
screens.layout: Strict single-column layout. Labels above inputs. Segmented controls for gender and skill level. A sticky 'Appliquer les filtres' CTA at the bottom above the home indicator, inside a surface container to block scrolling content.

screens.name: Profile
screens.purpose: Detailed view of the athlete's stats, bio, and video highlights.

states.empty: Icon + 'Profil non complet' + 'Compléter le profil' CTA.

screens.layout: Hero image at the top with subtle parallax. Deep black (surface) background below. Stats displayed in dense, condensed metrics blocks (using surfaceTertiary as chips). A pinned 'Contacter' CTA at the bottom.

screens.name: Messages
screens.purpose: Direct communication between players and recruiters.

states.empty: Message icon + 'Pas de messages' + 'Parcourir les profils'.

screens.layout: Standard chat interface. Messages from the user in surfaceTertiary, from the other party in brandTertiary. Input field at the bottom attached to the keyboard.

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the Dark-First Utility DARK guidelines. Do not use glass/blur effects; stick to solid `surfaceSecondary` for elevated cards and headers.
Ensure the UI is entirely in French as requested. For example, use 'Recruteurs', 'Athlètes', 'Rechercher', 'Messages'.

For the club logos (like PSG or Real Madrid), since PNG logos with transparency were not found via the image tool, implement the initials fallback explicitly: a `surfaceTertiary` circle with 2-3 letter initials (e.g., 'RMA' or 'PSG') in `onSurfaceTertiary`, weight 500. Do not use random placeholder URLs.

Implement the gradient scrim on every image that has text overlaid (especially in Onboarding and HomeFeed). The scrim must be a 3-stop vertical gradient from transparent -> ~20% surfaceInverse -> ≥70% surfaceInverse at the bottom.
Keep forms strictly single-column with labels above inputs. No floating labels. Ensure the primary CTA is always sticky at the bottom over scrolling content.
Use `Barlow Condensed` exclusively for headings, scores, metrics, and tight UI labels to enforce the sporty, athletic feel. Use `Manrope` for all readable body text.

No blue or purple anywhere in the app. The primary brand is Signal Red (`#FF453A`). If any status needs color, use the provided success/warning/info tokens. Info is intentionally metallic gray (`#8E8E93`).
